title: Argentine lawmakers travel to Brasília to repair relations with Brazil
content:
A delegation of Argentine deputies and senators from opposition parties will travel to Brasília next Wednesday with the aim of repairing bilateral relations, strained since President Javier Milei referred to his Brazilian counterpart, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, in offensive terms. The group is due to meet the Brazilian Senate's foreign relations committee, the foreign ministry and representatives of the presidency.
“We are travelling to Brasília to hold meetings within the framework of parliamentary diplomacy,” announced deputy Nicolás Massot, of the Encuentro Federal bloc, during a session of the Chamber of Deputies. He argued that “there is no electoral mandate, however strong, that allows the executive to trample forty years of strategic bilateral relations,” and described the deterioration of ties with the country's main trading partner as irresponsible.
Among the Argentine interests he considers to be at stake, Massot cited the functioning of Mercosur and Brazil's backing for Argentina's sovereignty claim over the Falklands.
The announcement came on the same day the Chamber of Deputies debated a proposed declaration condemning the insults and reaffirming the strategic character of the bilateral relationship, which also called for Foreign Minister Pablo Quirno to appear before Congress. The text received 128 votes in favour, 108 against and 9 abstentions. As it was not on the session's agenda, it required the backing of two-thirds of those present, and therefore failed despite holding a simple majority.
The crisis began on July 25, when Milei took part in São Paulo in the event proclaiming Flávio Bolsonaro as the Liberal Party's presidential candidate. There he referred to Lula as a “thief” and a “convict” and used disparaging language about a judge of Brazil's Supreme Federal Court. Brasília recalled its ambassador in Buenos Aires for consultations on July 26 and on August 4 downgraded relations to chargé d'affaires level, also requesting the return of Argentina's ambassador, who has not yet resumed his duties.
The composition of the delegation has not been finalised. Organisers expect the participation of lawmakers from the Unión Cívica Radical, the Socialist Party, the Coalición Cívica and the Partido Justicialista, among other forces, representing around 60% of the parties holding parliamentary seats. Massot stressed the initiative would be institutional in character and did not seek “any partisan intervention.”
The trip will take place a little over a month before Brazil's presidential elections, scheduled for October 4. The Argentine government has not commented on the initiative.

title: WLAK THE TALK: WHO Africa Health Leaders Take Health Commitments to the Streets of Addis Ababa
content:
WLAK THE TALK: WHO Africa Health Leaders Take Health Commitments to the Streets of Addis Ababa
Addis Ababa, August 23, 2026 (FMC) — Participants of the 76th Session of the World Health Organization (WHO) Regional Committee for Africa (RC76) took part in a symbolic health walk on Sunday from the Adwa Victory Memorial to Meskel Square in Addis Ababa, turning the “Walk the Talk” message into action while promoting physical activity and healthier lifestyles across Africa.
Ethiopia’s Health Minister Mekdes Daba, African health ministers, senior government officials, WHO leaders and prominent athletes, including Ethiopian Athletics Federation President Sileshi Sihine, participated in the event.
The initiative sought to translate health policies and commitments into practical action by encouraging people to incorporate regular physical activity into their daily lives and raising public awareness about preventing non-communicable diseases.
The walk began at the Adwa Victory Memorial, a landmark symbolizing Ethiopia’s historic victory and African resistance to colonialism, and proceeded through Addis Ababa’s pedestrian routes before concluding at Meskel Square.
Organizers emphasized that regular physical activity plays a vital role in reducing the risk of non-communicable diseases, including diabetes, hypertension and cardiovascular diseases, while contributing to healthier and more active communities.
The event also underscored Africa’s collective commitment to improving public health and the importance of moving beyond policy discussions toward tangible, everyday health practices.
The 76th Session of the WHO Regional Committee for Africa is scheduled to take place in Addis Ababa from August 24 to 28, 2026, bringing together more than 600 delegates, including health ministers and senior officials from the WHO African Region’s 47 member states, global health leaders, development partners, donors and WHO representatives.
During the five-day session, participants will assess progress toward regional health goals and deliberate on new strategies and resolutions.
The session is also expected to identify collective actions to strengthen health systems, advance universal health coverage, enhance health security and improve emergency preparedness across the continent.
The gathering is expected to provide a major platform for African countries and global health partners to deepen continental health cooperation and advance practical solutions to some of Africa’s most pressing health challenges.

title: California plug-in solar bill earns approval of both legislative houses
content:
California plug-in solar bill earns approval of both legislative houses
The California state Assembly has voted to pass Senate Bill 868, a bill that would allow the state’s residents to use portable solar generation devices with up to 1,200 W of output that plug into an electrical receptacle in a home or apartment.
The bill requires such devices to be used with the intent to offset the customer’s onsite electricity consumption and meet the standards of the most recent version of the National Electrical Code and the California Electrical Code. It also requires the systems to be certified by Underwriters Laboratories or an equivalent nationally recognized testing laboratory.
SB 868 would exempt users of these devices from requirements to file interconnection agreements with their local utility or to obtain the utility’s permission to use such devices, but it does allow a utility to require that customers notify it of their intent to use a plug-in solar device.
Notably, the text of SB 868 has been amended several times since the bill was introduced, adding language that removes as of January 1, 2030 the interconnection exemption and the rights of users to install the devices without utility permission.
The bill now heads to the Senate for concurrence on amendments made by the Assembly. If signed by the governor, the law would take effect on January 1, 2027.
Though the bill enjoyed broad support in both houses of the state legislature, it would not likely survive a veto by outgoing governor Gavin Newsom. Legislators in California have not attempted to override a governor’s veto since 1979.
Anticipation in the plug-in solar market
SB 868, which was introduced in January by Senator Scott Wiener, has become one of the most-watched pieces of plug-in solar legislation in the country. If passed, it would make California the eleventh state in the nation to enact such a law, opening a market for plug-in solar devices in the nation’s most populous state — and one where the cost of electricity is among the highest.
Both homeowners and renters could benefit from the ability to use plug-in solar devices to offset some of their consumption, potentially saving hundreds of dollars per year from a 1,200-watt setup as described in the bill.
SB 868 was backed by several prominent climate and energy groups, including the Environmental Working Group (EWG), The Sierra Club, Vote Solar, and nonprofit plug-in solar advocacy group Bright Saver.
In January 2026, Senator Wiener was joined by EWG California vice president Bernadette Del Chiaro and Bright Saver co-founder Cora Stryker in a webinar to celebrate the bill’s introduction and discuss the next steps.
“The nation is watching what happens in California,” said Stryker at the time. “If we get this across the finish line, the market will change permanently. We’ll have economies of scale. We’ll have manufacturers come into the American market, and it will never be the same.”
Following the bill’s passage out of the Assembly on August 25, EWG released a statement praising the state legislature’s efforts. “This is the most exciting clean energy idea around,” Del Chiaro said in the release. “With this bill, California is poised to fling its doors wide open to a real, tangible affordability solution for everyday consumers. Solar energy is a no-brainer for California and we applaud Sen. Wiener and his legislative colleagues for their hard work to put this critical clean energy solution on the governor’s desk.”

title: From ‘Madam Collector’ to ‘Collector Didi’, How Gargi Jain Is Keeping Tribal Girls in School
content: Every district collector's office has a chair reserved for visitors, but in Gujarat's Chhota Udepur, collector Gargi Jain chose a different one: a plastic chair inside a government school classroom, pulled up beside girls who had never had an officer of her rank sit down and simply listen. There was no inspection register, no entourage, just conversation. Today, those students do not call her "Madam Collector." They call her Collector Didi, and that shift in address has become the foundation of an initiative quietly reshaping how tribal girls in the district experience school. Jain, a 2015-batch IAS officer of the Gujarat cadre, took charge of Chhota Udepur, one of the state's most tribal-dominated districts, in February 2025. The district, home mainly to the Rathva community, was carved out of Vadodara district in 2013 and remains a place where girls are frequently the first in their families to attend school, with financial hardship, early marriage, and a lack of visible role models pushing many out of the classroom before they finish it. The pattern is not unique to Chhota Udepur; poverty and early marriage have long driven dropout across Gujarat's tribal belt, which is why sustained, trust-based outreach matters as much as scholarships or infrastructure. From "madam collector" to "collector didi" Jain calls the initiative ‘Collector in Classroom’. For the past year, she has set aside time every week to visit girls' schools across tribal blocks of the district, turning ordinary classrooms into spaces where students speak freely about their dreams, fears, and family pressures. "When I became the Collector of Chhota Udepur, I regularly started visiting schools attended by girls in tribal areas. I wanted these girls to know that their dreams are just as valid as anyone else's," she has said. In a district where girls often leave school early, Jain’s weekly visits are helping turn classrooms into spaces of confidence and possibility. The programme now directly mentors more than 750 girls across five Kanya Vidyalayas, joining a broader list of district collectors whose unconventional initiatives have reshaped local governance across India. Jain does not confine the sessions to academics. She speaks to the girls about life skills, communication, confidence, and legal rights, and fields questions ranging from the UPSC exam to engineering, medicine, and police services, not unlike collectors who have revived residential campuses for tribal children in Chhattisgarh's Dantewada district to keep them from dropping out. The story she waited years to tell The most defining part of each session is personal. Jain tells the girls about an incident from her own childhood, when a fellow bus passenger subjected her to inappropriate touch while she was travelling with her mother, an experience she carried silently for years without telling anyone. Sharing it now lets her explain the difference between good touch and bad touch and encourage the girls to speak up rather than stay silent, an approach that echoes how other officers have used braille-based lessons to bring visually impaired tribal children into government classrooms in Chhattisgarh. For many students in Chhota Udepur, it is the first time an adult in authority has spoken to them this openly about their own safety. From dropout numbers to a bigger dream The results are measurable. In 2025, nearly 9,000 children had dropped out of school across Chhota Udepur. By 2026, that number had fallen to around 5,500, with nearly 4,500 students returning to classrooms, an overall reduction of about 39%. Among girls specifically, the dropout rate fell by nearly 60% within a year, a decline achieved through a combination of government schemes and sustained outreach under Collector in Classroom. For Jain, the numbers are only part of the ambition. "I will not stop until five tribal girls become IAS officers," she has said, a goal that recalls how AI-based learning support has helped students across more than 350 government schools in Rajasthan's Tonk district build the confidence to keep pace with their studies. Every classroom visit brings that goal a little closer. Leadership is often measured in policy announcements and inaugurations, but Jain's initiative suggests it can also be measured in a chair pulled up beside a student instead of across a desk. If a girl from Chhota Udepur eventually walks into the Lal Bahadur Shastri National Academy of Administration as an IAS probationer, the journey will not have started at a coaching institute. It will have started in a tribal classroom, where a collector chose to listen before she chose to lead. Sources: 'IAS Gargi Jain's 'Collector in Classroom' Is Transforming Tribal Girls' Education in Gujarat': by Bhakti Kothari for Indian Masterminds, Published on August 2, 2026 'Gujarat's child brides can't avail govt scheme; they lead lives in desolation': by staff reporter for The Federal, Published on July 6, 2023

title: The impact of parathyroid hormone replacement with palopegteriparatide on synthesis of 1,25-dihydroxy vitamin D in hypoparathyroidism.
content: Parathyroid hormone (PTH) is the primary regulator of calcium and phosphate balance via direct action on the kidneys and bones and indirect action on the intestine. Hypoparathyroidism is caused by insufficient levels of PTH, leading to 1,25-dihydroxy vitamin D (1,25[OH]2D) deficiency. PTH-induced 1,25(OH)2D production is a highly regulated process essential for physiological functions that is reduced or absent in hypoparathyroidism. Physiological synthesis of 1,25(OH)2D requires 25-hydroxy vitamin D (25[OH]D) 1-α-hydroxylation via the renal CYP27B1 enzyme. Enzyme activity is dependent on CYP27B1 transcription, which is induced by specific PTH-1 receptor (PTH1R) activation that results in endosomal-derived intracellular cyclic adenosine monophosphate formation. Palopegteriparatide, a prodrug of PTH(1-34) used as replacement therapy in hypoparathyroidism, is designed to provide active PTH that exerts its physiological effect through the same affinity and binding to receptors as endogenous PTH. Throughout 3.5 years in the phase 3 PaTHway trial, 25(OH)D and 1,25(OH)2D levels were maintained within normal limits as a result of restoring endogenous production of 1,25(OH)2D and physiological signaling with palopegteriparatide treatment, thereby facilitating independence from active vitamin D. 1,25(OH)2D production can be compromised by even small changes to PTH that bias the physiological interaction between PTH and PTH1R. Thus, ensuring formation of 1,25(OH)2D should be a key outcome of interest in drug development of PTH replacement therapies. Data from clinical trials demonstrate active PTH released from palopegteriparatide interacts with PTH1R to ensure adequate 1,25(OH)2D synthesis, enabling independence from active vitamin D analogues, and confirms its position as a PTH replacement therapy.

title: Steuergelder für die Handyreparatur? Weshalb vom Zürcher Pilotprojekt auch ein Börsenkonzern profitiert
content:
Steuergelder für die Handyreparatur? Weshalb vom Zürcher Pilotprojekt auch ein Börsenkonzern profitiert
Geräte länger am Leben halten und so CO2 einsparen – die Grünen wollen einen Reparaturbonus für das ganze Land. Doch das Beispiel der Stadt Zürich zeigt: Repariert werden vor allem Handys, und manche werden dafür erst noch in einen anderen Kanton gefahren. Wie war das nochmals mit der Kreislaufwirtschaft?
Auf der Website der Stadt Zürich kann man live beobachten, wie Steuergelder verschwinden. Dort gibt eine Grafik an, wie viel Geld noch im städtischen Reparaturtopf vorhanden ist. Der Betrag schmilzt jedes Mal, wenn sich eine Zürcherin oder ein Zürcher dazu entscheidet, etwas Altes reparieren zu lassen statt fortzuschmeissen.
Eingeführt hat diesen Reparaturbonus der Zürcher Stadtrat erst vor wenigen Wochen. Wer in Zürich eine kaputte Kaffeemaschine, eine gerissene Hose oder ein defektes Handy reparieren lässt, bekommt Geld von der Stadt. Sie übernimmt 50 Prozent der Reparaturkosten, maximal 100 Franken sind es pro Person und Jahr. Knapp 3 Millionen Franken sind für das dreijährige Pilotprojekt vorgesehen. Vorerst sind nur Elektrogeräte und Textilien bonusberechtigt.
Dahinter steht das Prinzip der Kreislaufwirtschaft: Der Reparaturbonus soll dafür sorgen, dass weniger weggeworfen und mehr geflickt wird, und so das Klima schonen. Ähnliche Subventionen existieren in mehreren Westschweizer Gemeinden, die Grünen wollen das Prinzip auch schon national verankern. Doch jetzt zeigt der Zürcher Pilotbetrieb die Tücken der gutgemeinten Förderung auf.
Betrügerische Handyshops
Der Bonus wird derzeit nämlich vor allem für jene Geräte verwendet, bei denen eine Reparatur längst ein etabliertes Geschäft ist. Im Juli betrafen 78 Prozent der geförderten Reparaturaufträge Smartphones, Tablets oder Smartwatches, wie die Entsorgungs- und Recyclingabteilung ERZ auf Anfrage mitteilt. Sie relativiert sogleich: Betriebe für Smartphonereparaturen seien besonders schnell bei der Registrierung gewesen. Zudem sei die Aussagekraft der Daten noch gering.
Doch das Stichwort Handyreparaturen lässt aufhorchen. Österreich führte bereits 2022 einen grosszügigen Reparaturbonus ein. Im ersten Jahr entfielen rund 44 Prozent der Aufträge auf Smartphones. Später wurden Betrugsfälle bekannt, fast ausschliesslich in Handyshops. Medial wurde vom «Reparaturbonus-Betrug» gesprochen. Die Konsequenz: Österreich hat Smartphones und Tablets inzwischen von seiner «Geräte-Retter-Prämie» ausgeschlossen.
Die Stadt Zürich sagt, sie kenne die österreichischen Erfahrungen. Derzeit seien Reparaturen an Textilien und Elektrogeräten bonusberechtigt, weil diese Kategorien «den grössten ökologischen Nutzen» hätten. Man behalte sich aber vor, dies künftig anzupassen.
Und wie wappnet sich die Stadt gegen Betrug? Das simple Prinzip wirft jedenfalls Fragen auf. Kunden beziehen den Reparaturbonus online und bezahlen vor Ort den reduzierten Preis; der Betrieb erhält den fehlenden Betrag anschliessend von der Stadt zurückerstattet. Wer sich als Kunde registriert, muss allerdings bloss eine Postleitzahl und eine E-Mail-Adresse angeben. Es ist der Händler, der kontrolliert, ob man wirklich Zürcher Bürger ist. Und hier zeigt sich: Die Sicherheitsvorkehrungen sind minim. Als Wohnsitzbeleg reicht auch eine an sich selber adressierte Rechnung, die man ins Geschäft mitbringt.
Die Stadt räumt zudem ein, dass Mehrfachbezüge durch mehrere E-Mail-Adressen «technisch möglich» seien. Und es würde wohl auch nicht auffallen, wenn man eine Reparatur im Namen seiner Partnerin oder seines Partners tätigt. «Ein Nachweis, dass der Gegenstand tatsächlich durch die reparierende Person gekauft wurde, ist nicht Teil des Prüfprozesses und für den Umweltnutzen der Reparatur nicht wesentlich», schreibt ein ERZ-Sprecher dazu.
Förderung des Grossfilialisten
Betrugsrisiko hin oder her – Zürich hat ohnehin einen ganz anderen Fokus. Neben dem Klimaschutz geht es dem Stadtrat auch um Wirtschaftshilfe. «Wir bringen das Reparieren wieder in den Alltag und leisten einen Impuls für das lokale Gewerbe», so liess sich die zuständige SP-Stadträtin Simone Brandner in einer Medienmitteilung zitieren. Auch auf der Website wird der Reparaturbonus mit der Förderung des lokalen Gewerbes beworben.
Doch nun zeigt sich: Zu den teilnehmenden Betrieben gehört auch Mobilezone. Der börsenkotierte Telekomkonzern mit über 100 Millionen Franken Umsatz und 125 Filialen schweizweit bietet ausdrücklich Display- und Akkuwechsel an – laut Mobilezone «die beiden mit Abstand häufigsten Reparaturarten».
Somit fliesst städtisches Fördergeld nicht nur an kleine Quartiergeschäfte, sondern als indirekte Subvention auch an einen schweizweit tätigen Konzern. Noch bemerkenswerter ist, wohin ein Zürcher Handy via Mobilezone gelangt – aus der Stadt hinaus.
«Die in den Zürcher Shops angenommenen Geräte werden in unserer zentralen Werkstatt in Rotkreuz repariert», bestätigt Mobilezone auf Anfrage. In der Ortschaft im Kanton Zug betreibt das Unternehmen nach eigenen Angaben das grösste herstellerunabhängige Reparaturzentrum der Schweiz und setzt jährlich gegen 100 000 Geräte instand.
Eine Zürcherin gibt ihr Handy in der Filiale eines börsenkotierten Unternehmens ab, die Stadt übernimmt bis zu 100 Franken der Rechnung, und repariert wird anschliessend im Kanton Zug: Von dem Versprechen eines kleinräumigen, ökologischen Wirtschaftskreislaufs bleibt so nur wenig übrig. Das Departement von Simone Brander schreibt, es gehe darum, «das Reparieren an sich zu fördern». Dass der Bonus das lokale Gewerbe belebe, wie mehrfach versprochen, werde bloss noch als «willkommener Nebeneffekt» bezeichnet.
Mit oder wegen des Bonus?
Das Projekt in Zürich wird von Befürwortern der Kreislaufwirtschaft im ganzen Land genau verfolgt. Auch von Lisa Mazzone, Präsidentin der Grünen-Partei. Sie hatte schon vor einigen Jahren erfolglos versucht, Reparaturboni schweizweit einzuführen. Das Anliegen sei nach wie vor aktuell, sagt sie auf Anfrage. «Die Wegwerfwirtschaft schafft nur Abfallberge, die wir verhindern könnten», sagt Mazzone. «Wir werden deshalb wieder versuchen, das Recht auf Reparatur auf nationaler Ebene geltend zu machen.»
Wenn das Thema erneut auf die nationale Agenda gelangt, dürfte es auch um die Grundfrage solcher Ausschüttungen mit der Giesskanne gehen. Denn die Stadt Zürich rechnet mit rund 40 000 geförderten Reparaturen und somit 960 Tonnen eingespartem CO₂ – die Zahl leitet sie aus einer britischen Studie ab. Doch bezahlt der Staat tatsächlich für zusätzliche Reparaturen – oder subventioniert er Transaktionen, die ohnehin stattgefunden hätten?
Mitnahmeeffekte liessen sich «kaum verhindern» und seien «kaum objektiv messbar», räumt die Stadt Zürich ein. Auch am Ende des Pilotprojekts werde sich nicht eindeutig feststellen lassen, welche Reparaturen dank dem Bonus erfolgt seien und welche auch ohne ihn stattgefunden hätten. Befragungen sollen Hinweise liefern.
Andernorts ist das Instrument übrigens längst etabliert – und teilweise deutlich grosszügiger: Vevey am Genfersee zahlt seinen Bürgern bei einer Möbelreparatur bis zu 700 Franken. Zürich hat bei der Höhe seiner Subventionen also noch Luft nach oben.

title: En Chine, des succès littéraires venus du monde ouvrier et de la précarité
content: À la mi-juillet, Jibin Wang, un livreur de repas, s’est vu décerner l’un des prix littéraires les plus prestigieux de Chine pour un recueil de poèmes écrits entre deux courses. Dernier exemple en date de témoignages d’ouvriers sur leurs conditions de vie, une tradition souvent encadrée par les autorités qui remonte au début du lancement des réformes économiques dans les années 1980.

title: Gallery: Kino Sõprus brings cinema screenings to Lasnamäe

Gallery: Kino Sõprus brings cinema screenings to Lasnamäe
Kino Sõprus cinema chain showed its first film at Priisle Park in Tallinn's Lasnamäe district last week and is planning several outdoor screenings across the city in the coming weeks.
More than 400 viewers gathered in Priisle Park to watch Veiko Õunpuu's 2007 film "Sügisball" which was screened in Lasnamäe, where the acclaimed film was also shot.

title: Remains of Yehuda Katz, IDF soldier who went missing in 1982 battle, returned to Israel
content:
Remains of Yehuda Katz, IDF soldier who went missing in 1982 battle, returned to Israel
Bones belonging to Sgt. First Class Yehuda Katz are located in special operation led by military intelligence, Mossad; army doesn’t say where remains were located
- See more Times of Israel on Google - add us as a Preferred Source
Emanuel (Mannie) Fabian is The Times of Israel's military correspondent
The remains of Israeli soldier Sgt. First Class Yehuda Katz, who went missing in the First Lebanon War’s battle of Sultan Yacoub in 1982, were returned to Israel on Tuesday, the military announced, with Israeli leaders hailing the country’s commitment to bring back every missing or fallen soldier.
The battle, 44 years ago, was a skirmish between the Israel Defense Forces and the Syrian army in Lebanon’s Beqaa Valley. It claimed the lives of 21 Israeli servicemen and injured more than 30.
Katz, a tank soldier, went missing during the battle, along with Sgt. First Class Zachary Baumel and Sgt. First Class Zvi Feldman.
Baumel’s remains were recovered with Russian assistance and returned to Israel in 2019, and Feldman’s remains were recovered by Mossad agents in May 2025.
In a statement, the Israel Defense Forces said that in a special operation led by the Military Intelligence Directorate, in coordination with the Mossad spy agency, Katz’s bones were located and brought to Israel for burial. No details were given on where they were found.
The operation was based on intelligence obtained in recent months, according to the military. The IDF added that the finding was made possible due to a “series of intelligence and operational activities that continued for more than four decades, since he fell in battle.”
Earlier on Tuesday, the IDF said that personal findings belonging to Katz were brought back to Israel during the operation and given to his family for inspection. Meanwhile, Katz’s bones were taken for identification and confirmed on Tuesday evening to belong to the slain soldier.
The military said Katz’s family was updated over the years regarding the ongoing efforts to locate his remains and return them to Israel. “Upon completion of the mission, the family was informed of the return of their loved one. Unfortunately, Yehuda’s parents, Sarah and Yosef Katz, did not live to receive the news,” the army said.
In a statement, IDF Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir said, “The return of Yehuda Katz, the last fallen soldier from the Battle of Sultan Yacoub, is a significant moment for the IDF and for the State of Israel.”
“Decades have passed, but our duty toward our fallen has not changed. We will leave none of our people behind,” Zamir added.
The military chief later spoke with Katz’s family, which he told, “After 44 years, the Battle of Sultan Yacoub has come to an end.”
“All those missing from the battle have been returned to Israel. This is a special day for me, both as chief of the general staff and as a soldier of the Armored Corps,” Zamir was quoted as saying. “From the day I enlisted in the Armored Corps, I was raised on the legacy of that battle and on the moral commitment to bring all of our missing home. An entire nation stands united with you and shares in your emotion today.”
The IDF said Katz’s family thanked Zamir for the efforts to bring his remains to Israel for burial, and added that “his funeral would unite the entire nation and would be held in a manner reflecting his unique character.”
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said in a statement that he’d supported covert operations to locate the missing soldiers from Sultan Yacoub “for many years.”
He thanked the IDF, Mossad, Shin Bet, and the Missing Persons Directorate for their “determined and courageous work” to return Katz’s remains.
President Isaac Herzog, in his statement hailing the operation, which he said marked an end to “44 years of waiting, pain and longing.”
Herzog noted that he’d long kept a photo of Katz in his office, serving as “a daily reminder of our holy duty to return our sons home and not leave anyone behind.”
“Today I’m thinking in particular of his sister, Prichya, and the whole family,” the president said, in this “painful and emotional moment.”
“The State of Israel didn’t forget him and will never forget its children,” he said.
Defense Minister Israel Katz thanked “all the members of the defense establishment and the intelligence community, past and present, who have worked over the years with dedication and determination and never ceased their efforts until the mission was completed.”
There was no immediate statement from Katz’s family, who have been advocating for efforts to return the missing soldier’s remains for decades.
Rabbi Baruch Vider, the head of a prominent Jerusalem yeshiva, who also fought at Sultan Yacoub, spoke in a video shared by the Ynet news site: “For 44 years, I haven’t stopped praying for this day,” and went on to praise the fallen soldier as “a brilliant boy, a prodigy, humble, with great virtues.”
Times of Israel Staff contributed to this report

title: Belgium's fire of the century now 'under control'
content:
Belgium's largest wildfire in a century was brought "under control" Thursday after a seven-day fight involving hundreds of firefighters in the boggy terrain of the High Fens nature reserve.
"At this stage, the fire is now under control in its entirety and should no longer spread," barring a major change in weather conditions or other unforeseen factors, said the local governor's office.
The High Fens fire mushroomed over the weekend to half the size of Manhattan—3,000 hectares (7,500 acres)—charring a huge expanse of peatland, pine trees and hiking trails.
Firefighters brought "numerous flare-ups" under control overnight, working in very difficult conditions as powerful winds buffeted the eastern region bordering Germany—with a "mini-tornado" even striking a town outside the park.
But the governor's office said the fire was now fully contained on its western side, with operations continuing to the east to finish the job.
Seven aircraft from Germany, Norway, Belgium and Sweden were carrying out water drops in and around the burned perimeter, where ground temperatures remained "extremely high."
Aerial support crews, grounded by bad weather earlier in the week, hoped to keep operating until nightfall, when civil protection drones would take over the task of monitoring for "potential flare-ups," the governor's statement said.
It could take weeks or even months of soaking and dousing to prevent the High Fens blaze from reigniting, since the peatland terrain means fire can keep burning underground and resurface in a phenomenon known as a "zombie fire."
The spongy, highly flammable, carbon-rich material formed by decomposing plant matter is an ideal fuel for buried embers, which can lie dormant until favorable conditions, such as wind and dry weather, allow them to reignite in broad daylight.
"Forest workers who know the area like the back of their hand reckon we'll be monitoring this smoldering fire in the ground at least until the end of autumn," Nicolas Yernaux, a spokesman for the regional authorities, said earlier this week.
Around 350 firefighters and other emergency personnel remain deployed in the effort, as do the many farmers who mobilized in support of the operation since last week.
But authorities have lifted all evacuation orders in the border region since Wednesday, allowing the residents of several Belgian hamlets and a town on the German border to return home.
Germany's contingent of firefighters will start pulling out later Thursday, to be offset by Belgian firefighters, including volunteers, the governor's office said.
In another spot of good news, firefighters Thursday rescued a black grouse from the heart of the fire zone—an endangered species, with only 14 males and four or five females remaining in Belgium.
Climate debate
Europe has been swept by weeks of devastating wildfires fueled by dry conditions and a historically hot summer, with France, Greece, Portugal and Spain also battling major blazes.
Tackling the High Fens fire was made much harder by the fens' terrain—a patchwork of heath, peat bogs and raised wooden boardwalks.
The blaze broke out for reasons still unknown in an area that was ravaged by massive fires in 1911, during a similar period of heat waves.
It was the country's largest wildfire since then.
The combined shock of the fire and back-to-back heat waves has ignited a debate over whether Belgium is sufficiently prepared for the effects of climate change.
Interior Minister Bernard Quintin mounted a lengthy defense of the government's response during a grilling before the Belgian Parliament on Thursday afternoon.
"We are facing risks that are becoming increasingly complex and potentially large-scale," he said, pledging a national resilience plan to address climate-related threats.
Opposition parties accuse the government of failing to allocate enough resources to tackling wildfires, noting that Belgium has no aerial firefighting capability of its own.
But the government rejects the criticism, arguing that it has invested in ground-based resources, which it says are more effective, and purchased helicopters for water-bombing operations, with deliveries of the aircraft under way.

title: Cholesterol medicines during pregnancy: Do they increase birth defect risk?
content:
For many years, women were generally advised to avoid statins during pregnancy. The concern was that these cholesterol-lowering medicines might interfere with foetal development and increase the risk of birth defects.
However, evidence from human studies has gradually challenged that assumption. An updated systematic review and meta-analysis have now brought together data from 21 studies involving more than 3.1 million pregnancies to take another look at the safety of statin exposure during pregnancy. The findings are broadly reassuring: the researchers did not find an increased risk of congenital malformations among women who were exposed to statins during pregnancy. But the findings also suggest that the question is more complicated than simply deciding whether statins are “safe” or “unsafe” during pregnancy.
“Our updated systematic review and meta-analysis provide considerable reassurance on this question, but it should not be interpreted as a reason to prescribe statins routinely during pregnancy,” says Dr Saptarshi Bhattacharya, senior endocrinologist, Apollo Hospital, Delhi, who was in the review team of endocrinologists.
Statins are commonly prescribed to lower bad cholesterol and reduce the risk of cardiovascular disease. This is important for women who already have significant heart disease or other cardiovascular risk factors. Pregnancy itself places additional demands on the cardiovascular system. Changes in blood flow, blood vessels and the body’s tendency to form clots can create additional challenges for women who already have cardiovascular disease.
Historically, concerns about possible foetal harm meant that statins were generally stopped during pregnancy. But stopping cardiovascular medications is not necessarily risk-free for every woman. When the mother’s cardiovascular risk is high, could continuing treatment sometimes provide important benefits?
“We analysed 21 studies, including six randomised trials, involving 9,016 pregnancies exposed to statins and more than 3.1 million without statin exposure. Overall, statin use was not associated with an increased risk of congenital malformations. The odds ratio was 1.05, with the confidence interval ranging from 0.92 to 1.21. There was also no signal for specific organ malformations,” says Dr Bhattacharya.
The size of the dataset makes the absence of an overall increase in congenital malformations reassuring. Importantly, the findings were consistent across different analyses, including randomised trials and observational studies. But “no evidence of increased risk” should not be interpreted as proof of zero risk. “Statin exposure during pregnancy remains relatively uncommon and some individual statins have been studied much less extensively than others. A very small increase in risk, or a rare specific foetal abnormality, could therefore escape detection. We still need larger trials,” says Dr Bhattacharya.
Statin exposure was not associated with a significant increase in low birth weight. “However, when we looked specifically at cohort studies, low birth weight was more frequent among statin-exposed pregnancies. The signal was largely seen with a particular type, what we call non-pravastatin statins (as opposed to pravastatin, which is a low-to-moderate intensity statin).
There are biological reasons why pravastatin has attracted particular interest in pregnancy, including its relatively water-soluble nature. It has also been studied specifically in pregnancy complications such as pre-eclampsia. However, the available evidence is not sufficient to conclude that pravastatin is definitively safer than other statins. “Comparisons between individual drugs are based on smaller numbers and are influenced by why each statin was prescribed,” explains Dr Bhattacharya.
He is also cautious because women taking statins may already have diabetes, hypertension, vascular disease or other metabolic problems that themselves influence foetal growth. This is known as confounding by indication: the reason a woman needs treatment may partly explain the outcome attributed to the treatment.
The analysis also did not find a statistically significant increase in preterm delivery among women exposed to statins.
Women who require statins are different from women who do not. “In our analysis, they were older and more likely to have diabetes, hypertension, cardiovascular disease and a history of smoking. Separating the effect of the drug from that of the underlying disease is therefore difficult, particularly in observational studies,” says Dr Bhattacharya
For most women taking statins for primary prevention or uncomplicated high cholesterol, stopping treatment during pregnancy remains reasonable. Pregnancy is a limited period, and the immediate cardiovascular consequences of temporarily withholding therapy are generally small.
“But the equation may be very different for a woman with established cardiovascular disease or very severe inherited hypercholesterolaemia. For a woman at very high cardiovascular risk, stopping effective lipid-lowering treatment for pregnancy and breastfeeding may not always be harmless,” Dr Bhattacharya.
The decision, he feels, should balance two risks: the uncertain foetal risk of continuing treatment against the maternal cardiovascular risk of stopping it. “Our results provide reassurance for situations in which continued statin therapy is considered necessary, rather than supporting routine statin treatment during pregnancy,” he says.
The major unanswered question is no longer simply whether statins cause birth defects. “We need better information on which women may benefit from continuing treatment, which statin should be used, at what dose and during which part of pregnancy. Large prospective studies should examine individual statins separately and carefully document the timing and duration of exposure. They should also evaluate foetal growth, preterm delivery, placental outcomes and longer-term development of children exposed in utero,” says Dr Bhattacharya. As of now, the review just challenges the older assumption that they must invariably be avoided in every pregnant woman.

title: Более 5 тысяч детей военнослужащих отдохнули в бесплатном лагере семьи Лабазюк в Хмельницкой области
content:
В Хмельницкой области завершилась последняя смена летнего сезона в национально-патриотическом лагере "Eco-life Збруч". На этот раз здесь отдохнули более 100 детей военнослужащих. С момента открытия лагеря в 2022 году его смены посетили уже более 5 тысяч детей. Для семей участие бесплатное – расходы на проживание, питание и программу берет на себя благотворительный фонд семьи Лабазюк "Мы рядом". Репортаж об отдыхе детей защитников был показан в эфире информационного телемарафона "Единые новости".
Инициатором создания лагеря является Сергей Лабазюк, основатель благотворительного фонда. Идея появилась после начала полномасштабной войны: дать детям защитников место, где они хотя бы на несколько дней могут отвлечься от тревог, новостей с фронта и постоянного ожидания звонка от отца или матери.
"Я, как отец двоих детей, понимаю, что сегодня у нас катастрофа с гаджетами, и дети мало общаются между собой. Здесь задача состояла в том, чтобы было общение, чтобы было движение. А это спортивные, игровые и другие занятия. И, конечно, патриотизм", – говорит Сергей Лабазюк.
Лагерь обустроили в Хмельницкой области, на берегу реки Збруч. Лагерь создавали с нуля: жилые дома, спортивные площадки, зоны для активного отдыха, бассейны и пространство для занятий и вечерних мероприятий. Программа построена так, чтобы у детей почти не оставалось времени на переживания по поводу войны: спорт, командные игры, квесты, творческие мастер-классы, походы, водные развлечения, экскурсии, вечера у костра и совместные праздники.
Отдельное направление – национально-патриотическое воспитание. К детям приезжают ветераны и военные, проводят мастер-классы, беседуют с подростками о службе, взаимопомощи, ответственности и опыте защиты страны. В других сменах к программе также присоединялись пограничники, спасатели и правоохранители. Для организаторов принципиально важно, чтобы патриотическая составляющая не превращалась в формальность, а строилась на живом общении с людьми, имеющими собственный опыт войны.
Благотворительный фонд "Мы рядом" работает с 2012 года. Среди направлений помощи фонда и партнерских проектов – закупка техники, беспилотников, Starlink, зарядных станций и медикаментов для военных, поддержка медицинских учреждений и детских проектов.

title: Knochen eines seit 1991 Vermissten auf Innsbrucks Nordkette entdeckt
content:
Knochen eines seit 1991 Vermissten auf Innsbrucks Nordkette entdeckt
Ein Knochenfund auf der Innsbrucker Nordkette hat nach 35 Jahren zur Identifizierung eines seit 1991 vermissten Südtirolers geführt.
Ein Knochen eines bereits seit 1991 abgängigen, damals 22-jährigen Südtirolers ist Ende Juni von einem Wanderer in einer „Schotterreise“ im Bereich der „Vorderen Brandjochspitze“ auf der Innsbrucker Nordkette gefunden worden.
DNA-Untersuchung identifiziert vermissten Südtiroler
Durch eine von der Innsbrucker Gerichtsmedizin durchgeführte DNA-Untersuchung konnte der Knochen dem Mann zugeordnet werden, berichtete die Polizei am Mittwoch. Darüber hinaus wurden weitere zehn Knochen gefunden, die aber Tieren zuzurechnen waren.
Große Suchaktion blieb 1991 erfolglos
Da man den Südtiroler Alpinisten bereits 1991 – nach einer Abgängigkeitsanzeige – im Bereich der Nordkette vermutet hatte, wurde damals eine groß angelegte Suchaktion gestartet.
Diese führte jedoch zu keinem Erfolg – bis zum 21. Juni dieses Jahres, als der 42-Jährige auf die Knochen stieß. Nicht mehr feststellen ließ sich indes die Todesursache. Es gebe aber keine Indizien für Fremdverschulden, hieß es.

title: ‘Pay back the money’: Nkandla architect ordered to repay over R147m with interest
content:
Minenhle Makhanya authorised non-security upgrades, including a swimming pool, tunnels and lifts, causing costs to balloon from R27.8 million to R216 million.
The Special Investigating Unit (SIU) has secured a judgment by the Special Tribunal ordering Minenhle Makhanya, the former architect and principal agent responsible for the security upgrades at former President Jacob Zuma’s Nkandla residence, to pay the National Treasury more than R147 million.
The amount represents the financial loss suffered by the Department of Public Works (DPW) as a result of unlawful conduct in the project.
Millions
Makhanya was ordered to pay R147 269 444.06, an amount which the SIU said represents the financial loss suffered by the DPW due to unlawful conduct in the project. He was also ordered to pay the costs of the legal proceedings, including the costs of two counsels.
The judgment, delivered on Wednesday, 26 August 2026, found that Makhanya’s appointment and subsequent conduct in the Nkandla upgrades were unlawful and resulted in significant financial loss to the State.
The Tribunal further ordered that the repayment will accrue interest at 11.25% per annum from the date of judgment.
Initial costs
The investigation into the Nkandla security upgrades was authorised in terms of Proclamation R59 of 2013, which directed the SIU to investigate allegations relating to DPW’s procurement and to recover financial losses.
Following Zuma’s election as President, the South African Police Service (Saps) and South African National Defence Force (SANDF) conducted security assessments and identified additional measures.
Based on these assessments, DPW initially determined the project cost at R27 893 067.46, which was authorised on 11 August 2009.
DPW was required to procure goods and services in accordance with procurement laws. Project manager DJ Rindel appointed Makhanya as principal agent on 27 August 2009.
The Tribunal found that his appointment was not preceded by a competitive bidding process, that there was no lawful justification for bypassing procurement requirements, and that Makhanya was not listed as a supplier with DPW.
Escalation of costs
The SIU investigation found that Makhanya authorised and oversaw works beyond the security measures identified by Saps and SANDF. The project cost escalated from R27.8 million to R216,010,478.24.
Structures authorised included tunnels with exits and lifts, 20 accommodation units for Saps and SANDF, a laundry facility, a visitors’ lounge, basement clinic parking, VIP parking, a fire pool, relocation of households, internal roads, air‑conditioning, and landscaping, totalling R68 506 106.
The Tribunal found Makhanya authorised and certified payments for structures not required by security assessments, failed to obtain written approvals for variations, certified payments above market costs, and approved payments for incomplete or unaccounted work.
He authorised payments to Moneymine Investments 310 CC and Bonelena Construction and Projects (Pty) Ltd amounting to R54 825 513, contrary to contract provisions.
Tribunal findings
The Tribunal found Makhanya breached statutory, professional and contractual obligations under the Architectural Profession Act, the Code of Professional Conduct, DPW’s Manual for Architects, and the JBCC agreement.
Defences raised by Makhanya, including claims he acted under Saps and SANDF instructions and arguments on prescription, were rejected.
“It is regrettable that the first defendant (Makhanya) stands alone as the person against whom the SIU has launched action, as he clearly did not act alone in allowing the costs of the upgrade at Nkandla to balloon,” Judge K. Pillay stated.
“However, as architect and principal agent, he bore the responsibility to ensure that the second defendant (DPW) did not incur fruitless and wasteful expenditure.”
The Tribunal declared invalid the contract concluded by or on behalf of the then Director‑General of DPW in relation to Makhanya’s appointment and ordered him to pay legal costs, including two counsels. The ruling runs to 73 pages, detailing breaches and obligations.
Recovery
The SIU accepted Makhanya’s submission reducing the claim by R7.8 million, which Zuma repaid for non‑security upgrades. This amount will be deducted from the total repayment.
The Tribunal’s orders form part of the SIU’s mandate to recover public funds lost through unlawful conduct. In line with the Special Investigating Units and Special Tribunals Act 74 of 1996, the SIU will refer any evidence of criminal conduct uncovered during its investigation to the National Prosecuting Authority.
The Nkandla upgrades were previously the subject of the Public Protector’s 2014 report Secure in Comfort, which found Zuma unduly benefited. The Constitutional Court later ordered Zuma to repay R7.8 million, and the phrase “pay back the money” became a rallying cry in Parliament.

title: Libye : un projet d’accord paraphé à Tunis pour relancer le processus électoral
content:
Libye : un projet d’accord paraphé à Tunis pour relancer le processus électoral
Des représentants des autorités de l’Est et de l’Ouest libyens ont paraphé jeudi 20 août à Tunis un projet d’accord sous l’égide de la Mission des Nations unies en Libye (Manul), centré sur la Haute commission nationale électorale et le cadre juridique des futurs scrutins, une étape présentée comme un progrès vers des élections nationales encore attendues dans le pays.
Selon The Libya Observer, qui cite la Manul, le texte a été élaboré par le comité dit « 4+4 », chargé de traiter les deux premiers volets de la feuille de route onusienne : la recomposition du conseil de la commission électorale et la révision des lois électorales encadrant les élections présidentielle et législatives.
Les membres du comité doivent se retrouver de nouveau en Libye avant la fin du mois d’août pour arrêter les modalités d’application du texte et en faire l’annonce officielle. L’accord n’est donc pas encore mis en œuvre et ne règle pas, à ce stade, l’ensemble du contentieux institutionnel libyen.
Deux jours plus tôt, la cheffe de la mission onusienne, Hanna Tetteh, avait déclaré devant le Conseil de sécurité que le processus entrait dans une « phase critique », alors que la mission poursuivait à Tunis un nouveau cycle de discussions pour tenter de sortir de l’impasse entre la Chambre des représentants et le Haut Conseil d’État.
Les négociations actuelles s’inscrivent dans une séquence engagée au printemps. Le 29 avril, un premier round tenu à Rome avait acté, selon la Manul, le principe d’une recomposition du conseil de la Haute commission électorale, avec la désignation de six membres par les deux chambres et la recommandation de confier la présidence de l’instance à un magistrat proposé par le procureur général.
Le 15 juillet, l’agence de presse libyenne LANA rapportait que la mission onusienne avait intégré la majorité des points déjà validés dans un projet de texte et fixé le début août comme échéance pour reprendre les discussions à Tunis. Le 6 août, la Manul a ensuite indiqué, toujours selon The Libya Observer, qu’un mécanisme de consensus avait été arrêté pour la désignation du futur président de la commission électorale.
Les États-Unis ont salué ces progrès le 22 août. D’après l’ambassade américaine en Libye, ils constituent une étape importante vers un chemin crédible menant à des élections nationales, tandis que Washington dit vouloir poursuivre son soutien au dialogue mené avec l’ONU et ses partenaires internationaux.

title: Emissioni auto, perché le elettriche migliorano la salute dei bambini nelle grandi città
content:
Uno studio di The Lancet dimostra come il calo dei gas di scarico favorisca il recupero della funzionalità polmonare nei più piccoli, confermando i benefici della mobilità a zero emissioni
Zona a basse emissioni, l’esempio di Londra
Ridurre l’inquinamento delle città abbassando le emissioni climalteranti e nocive delle auto a combustione interna, fa bene alla salute dei bambini. Ovviamente non solo a loro ma anche a tutti gli abitanti delle metropoli urbani, ma uno studio scientifico pubblicato su The Lancet Public Health, che ha per protagonista il centro di Londra, ci fornisce una certezza in più.
Nella capitale inglese è stata creata una zona a basse emissioni, chiamata ULEZ, acronimo di Ultra Low Emission Zone, la più grande area urbana al mondo per testare sul campo l’impatto dell’inquinamento prodotto dai veicoli sulla salute dei più piccoli fino ai 9 anni anni. In seguito allo studio quinquennale dal titolo Children’s Health in London and Luton, infatti, sono stati analizzati i miglioramenti della qualità dell’aria.
Meglio Londra o Luton?
I risultati degli studi (condotti da ricercatori della Queen Mary University di Londra) ci dicono che il miglioramento della qualità dell’aria ha contribuito a ripristinare la crescita polmonare precedentemente compromessa dall’esposizione all’inquinamento atmosferico. Gli accademici hanno “selezionato” 3.400 bambini delle scuole elementari, provenienti da 84 istituti londinesi e della cittadina di Luton, usata come sito di controllo per via di una simile combinazione di inquinanti del traffico, ma priva di zona a basse emissioni.
Come si è svolta la ricerca
Mentre nel 2019 è iniziata l’attività di filtro della ULEZ fino a coprire tutta l’area nel 2023, dal 2018 al 2022, durante le visite scolastiche annuali, sono state misurate e monitorate le dimensioni e la salute dei polmoni dei bambini al fine di valutare l’impatto dei cambiamenti nella qualità dell’aria sul loro sviluppo polmonare.
Analizzando i dati raccolti nell’arco di 5 anni, il team ha scoperto che, dopo l’implementazione della ULEZ le dimensioni e la salute dei polmoni dei bambini londinesi sono migliorate rapidamente, raggiungendo livelli paragonabili a quelli dei bambini di Luton. Ancora più importante, hanno dimostrato che questi miglioramenti nella crescita polmonare erano strettamente correlati al miglioramento della qualità dell’aria successiva all’implementazione della ULEZ. Questa barriera urbana che obbliga al pagamento di 12,50 sterline al giorno per circolare nella zona ha avuto conseguenze ben tangibili avendo ridotto il traffico veicolare, soprattutto auto più vecchie, quindi poco efficienti.
Cosa dimostra lo studio
Il team ha valutato la salute e lo sviluppo polmonare dei bambini misurando con precisione il loro volume espiratorio forzato in un secondo, ovvero la quantità di aria che può essere espirata forzatamente dai polmoni dopo un’inspirazione massimale, in relazione all’esposizione al biossido di azoto, l’inquinante più rappresentativo dell’inquinamento da gas di scarico.
I ricercatori hanno scoperto che nei cinque anni successivi all’introduzione della ULEZ, l’esposizione dei bambini londinesi al biossido di azoto è diminuita due volte più velocemente e in misura più che doppia rispetto a quella dei bambini di Luton. Hanno quindi dimostrato che, al diminuire dell’esposizione al biossido di azoto, il volume espiatorio dei piccoli londinesi aumentava di 10 ml all’anno in più rispetto ai bambini di Luton. Al termine dei cinque anni il valore era lo stesso per i bambini di Londra e Luton, indicando che la crescita polmonare dei bambini londinesi si era accelerata durante i cinque anni per “recuperare” il divario con il gruppo di controllo di Luton.
Nel corso dello studio, il team ha osservato che la percentuale di bambini con funzionalità polmonare clinicamente compromessa è diminuita dal 14% al 9% a Londra, rispetto a una diminuzione dal 9% al 7% a Luton. Infatti, il mancato raggiungimento del pieno sviluppo polmonare entro la prima età adulta aumenta il rischio che i bambini sviluppino malattie respiratorie, malattie cardiovascolari e metaboliche e morte prematura in età adulta. Questi risultati, che dimostrano come i deficit nella crescita e nella salute polmonare dei bambini possano essere corretti, hanno pertanto importanti implicazioni per il miglioramento della salute a lungo termine dei bambini.
Il professor Chris Griffiths, docente di medicina generale presso l’Università di Oxford e la Queen Mary University di Londra, coautore senior dello studio, ha dichiarato: “L’inquinamento atmosferico causato dal traffico nelle città danneggia la salute e lo sviluppo dei bambini. Forniamo le prove più solide finora disponibili su come prevenire questi danni. L’istituzione di zone a basse emissioni, con obiettivi ambiziosi, dovrebbe essere considerata una priorità per le città di tutto il mondo che soffrono di inquinamento atmosferico legato al traffico“.
Auto elettriche fanno bene alla salute
Insomma, forzando il concetto, ma neanche troppo in verità, possiamo considerare che l’auto elettrica sarebbe un toccasana per la salute della popolazione giovane e adulta perché sarebbe il contributo più importante nelle affollate metropoli europee ed italiane, alla riduzione di emissioni nocive per la salute umana e dell’ambiente. Infatti, ulteriori dati evidenziano che con l’estensione del traffico limitato la riduzione di NO2 raggiunge il 54%, contro il 27% dello scenario senza l’estensione della ULEZ.
Sebbene la ricerca inglese non si focalizzi unicamente sui veicoli elettrici, è proprio in questo contesto che l’elettrico mostra i suoi punti di forza principali. Ma non è ancora tutto. Non bisogna sottovalutare l’inquinamento acustico ridotto, perché la silenziosità del motore è particolarmente apprezzabile alle basse velocità del traffico cittadino. Ed il fatto che la frenata rigenerativa limita l’uso dei freni tradizionali, riducendo le polveri sottili generate dal consumo delle pastiglie.

title: Eye microsurgery in Novosibirsk popular among Kyrgyzstanis
content:
Citizens of Kyrgyzstan with complex eye conditions seek treatment at the Novosibirsk branch of the Interdisciplinary Scientific and Technical Complex (ISTC) Eye Microsurgery. Medical Center Director Valery Chernykh said during a press tour for journalists from Kyrgyzstan, Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan.
According to him, before the COVID-19 pandemic, patients from 38 countries sought treatment at the center, which performed around 3,000 surgeries annually.
In 2025, the top five countries by the number of foreign patients included Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan and Azerbaijan.
About half of the Kyrgyz patients remained at the clinic for treatment after undergoing diagnostic examinations.
Valery Chernykh noted that patients from Kyrgyzstan seek care for serious conditions, including retinal detachment and post-traumatic eye problems.
The Novosibirsk branch of the ISTC Eye Microsurgery has nine departments.
The medical center’s distinctive feature is its ability to handle large numbers of patients. In 2025, about 50,000 surgeries were performed there, with 80 percent classified as high-complexity surgical procedures.
The medical center also successfully operates a doctor-to-doctor telemedicine project, which allows specialists to hold consultations to determine whether treatment is possible. Ophthalmologists from different regions of Russia regularly seek expert consultations from specialists at the Novosibirsk branch of the ISTC.
The center also offers so-called «live surgery,» allowing unique surgical procedures to be broadcast in real time. The technology is also used for research and educational purposes.
Valery Chernykh added that doctors from Kyrgyzstan and other Central Asian countries come to the clinic for internships.

title: „Haben vorgesorgt“ - Gasspeicher in Österreich zu zwei Dritteln befüllt
content:
Auch wenn die Gasspeicher in Österreich mit 65,73 Prozent (26.8.) derzeit etwas geringer befüllt sind als vor einem Jahr, sind damit 78 Prozent eines durchschnittlichen Jahresverbrauchs eingelagert. Im europäischen Vergleich sind die hiesigen Speicher gut gefüllt, betont Wirtschaftsminister Wolfgang Hattmannsdorfer (ÖVP).
Vor einem Jahr (26. August 2025) waren die Speicher in Österreich mit 81 Prozent noch stärker gefüllt, zeigt ein Blick auf die Daten der Austrian Gas Grid Management (AGGM). In der Energiekrise 2021 war sie noch nicht einmal bei 50 Prozent und erreichte das ganze Jahr über keine 60 Prozent – trotzdem war die Versorgung stabil.
Betrachtet man den Befüllungsdurchschnitt der vergangenen sieben Jahre am 26. August, so liegt dieser laut Berechnungen auf Basis der AGGM-Daten bei 78,1 Prozent.
Durch US-Iran-Krieg gestiegener Gaspreis hemmte Befüllung
Fachleute führen den heuer etwas geringeren Füllstand verglichen zum Vorjahr auf die Gaspreise zurück, die just angestiegen sind, als die Zeit der Einspeicherung heuer begann. Grund dafür war der US-israelische Krieg mit dem Iran. Während Österreich dank der hohen Speicherkapazitäten trotzdem versorgungssicher ist, gab es in Deutschland zuletzt bereits den Aufruf der dortigen Bundesregierung an die Marktbeteiligten, die dort recht leeren Speicher rasch vor der kalten Jahreszeit aufzufüllen.
Derzeit liegt der Preis für eine Megawattstunde Gas bei 66 Euro an der Börse. Vor einem Jahr waren es noch 33 Euro.
„Österreich hat vorgesorgt und ist bei der Gasversorgung besser aufgestellt als viele andere europäische Länder“, meinte Hattmannsdorfer am Mittwoch. „Unsere Speicher können mehr Gas aufnehmen, als Österreich in einem Jahr verbraucht. Diese starke Speicherinfrastruktur und die Strategische Gasreserve geben uns Versorgungssicherheit und sind ein klarer Wettbewerbsvorteil für unseren Standort.“
Hiesiger Jahresverbrauch bei 75 bis 80 TWh
Der Speicherstand von rund 66 Prozent entspricht etwa 66 Terawattstunden (TWh) Gas, die gesamte Speicherkapazität beträgt 100 TWh. Der Jahresverbrauch in Österreich lag zuletzt zwischen 75 und 80 TWh.
Der Grad der Einspeicherung beträgt laut Hattmannsdorfer europaweit derzeit durchschnittlich etwa 62 Prozent und ist damit geringer als hierzulande, „obwohl Österreich im Vergleich zu anderen EU-Ländern über besonders große Speicherkapazitäten verfügt“. Der Politiker verweist in Bezug auf die Versorgungssicherheit für Haushalte und Industrie auch auf die strategische Gasreserve, verpflichtende Gasvorräte für Kraftwerke sowie besonders geschützte Reserven von Industriebetrieben. Die strategische Gasreserve war wie berichtet zuletzt bis April 2029 verlängert worden.
Experte zuversichtlich für Versorgungssicherheit
„Gasspeicher sind insbesondere in der kalten Jahreszeit und bei höherem Verbrauch relevant“, erinnert Christoph Dolna-Gruber von der Energieagentur in Unterlagen des Wirtschaftsministeriums vom Donnerstag. „Die aktuell in Österreich bereits gespeicherten Gasmengen in Kombination mit stabilen Importen und verstärkter inländischer Erzeugung in Wittau lassen uns zuversichtlich in den Winter blicken.“

content: Það var mikið fjölmenni á sveitahátíðinni Grímsævintýri á Borg í Grímsnesi í dag. Þetta er líka bara þannig að kynslóðirnar eru að koma hingað margar saman. title: Dudamel cierra una era de 17 años que transformó la Filarmónica de Los Ángeles
content:
Tras un histórico ciclo de 17 años, Gustavo Dudamel cerró anoche su etapa al frente de la Filarmónica de Los Ángeles (LA Phil), consolidando una simbiosis cultural que transformó la música clásica en Estados Unidos, diversificó las audiencias e impulsó la integración de la comunidad latina.
El broche de oro final tuvo lugar el 23 de agosto con un concierto benéfico en el Hollywood Bowl destinado a la recaudación de fondos para Venezuela, poniendo fin a una historia iniciada en 2009, cuando asumió la batuta de la orquesta angelina.
Su llegada se sumó a la trayectoria de una institución que ya destacaba en la programación contemporánea bajo las gestiones de sus predecesores, el indio Zubin Mehta y el finlandés Esa-Pekka Salonen.
Es en esa dimensión donde el director venezolano impregnó a la orquesta de su sello característico: una energía desbordante y un rigor técnico que transformaron la ejecución sinfónica en un puente intergeneracional.
Pero LA Phil y Dudamel no serían lo mismo sin su apuesta por una mayor diversidad, que incluyó a compositores latinoamericanos en sus programas, como el mexicano Arturo Márquez o el argentino Alberto Ginastera.
Fruto de esta transformación, el Walt Disney Concert Hall de Los Ángeles, hogar de la institución, acercó la música clásica a la enorme comunidad latina que habita en el sur de California.
Esta evolución consolidó “una solidez y un equilibrio de sonido únicos” que impulsaron a la institución a trascender los escenarios habituales, según dijo el crítico musical Alex Ross en declaraciones a la emisora de radio KRCW.
La formación logró un hito inédito al convertirse en la primera orquesta en ofrecer su propio set en el Festival de Coachella.
Su actuación se convirtió en una de las más originales del festival, el más grande de EE UU, al fusionar el rap con clásicos de cine o el reguetón junto a célebres cantantes como Becky G, Ca7riel & Paco Amoroso o Cynthia Erivo.
El alcance de Dudamel y la LA Phil también quedó patente en la histórica actuación en la final del Mundial de fútbol del pasado julio, compartiendo cartel con figuras de gran alcance como Madonna, BTS, Shakira y Justin Bieber.
Otra ocasión en la que desplegó su arsenal comandando el icónico himno deportivo “Seven Nation Army” con la orquesta, una actuación enmarcada en una de sus múltiples iniciativas solidarias para recaudar fondos para el terremoto de su país.
Más allá de la música
Más allá de la repercusión mundial que ha logrado alcanzar el director de orquesta venezolano con la LA Phil, la institución consolidó iniciativas como Youth Orchestra Los Ángeles (YOLA), un programa con el que brindó formación musical gratuita a jóvenes de bajos ingresos de California.
Este proyecto se inspiró en “El Sistema”, el renombrado modelo pedagógico y social fundado en Venezuela que instauró José Antonio Abreu en 1975 para la inclusión y el desarrollo comunitario: fue su manera de devolver el favor a aquel programa que apostó por su talento en su juventud y que lo llevó a ser quien es.
Este septiembre de 2026, Dudamel asumirá oficialmente como director musical y artístico de la Filarmónica de Nueva York (NY Phil).

title: Bart, Guido, Jeaninne en Bernard van woonzorgcentrum 't Hoge genieten op eerste rij van Willy Sommers op Kamping Kitsch in Kortrijk
content:
Bart, Guido, Jeaninne en Bernard van woonzorgcentrum 't Hoge in Kortrijk zijn vandaag de eregasten op Kamping Kitsch in Kortrijk. Samen met hun begeleiders mogen ze het optreden van Willy Sommers op de eerste rij meemaken. "Het is al 50 jaar geleden dat ik me nog zó heb geamuseerd", zegt Guido.
Bart, Guido, Jeaninne en Bernard van woonzorgcentrum 't Hoge genieten op eerste rij van Willy Sommers op Kamping Kitsch in Kortrijk
Het geluk van Bart, Guido, Jeaninne en Bernard van woonzorgcentrum 't Hoge in Kortijk kan niet op vandaag. Zij mogen naar Willy Sommers gaan kijken op Kamping Kitsch in Kortijk.
In volle ornaat - zoals dat hoort - kwamen de bewoners vanmiddag met hun begeleiders aan op het festival om er een mooie dag te beleven.
"Het is een zotte ingeving geweest om de bewoners naar hier mee te nemen", zegt Ilse Flockmans, directeur van het woonzorgcentrum. "Uiteraard hebben we alles goed voorbereid en zijn de families van de bewoners ook op de hoogte. Iedereen heeft er heel veel zin in."
En dat ze er zin in hebben, dat beamen de bewoners zelf. "Heel tof, het is mijn eerste keer hier op Kamping Kitsch", zegt Bart. "Het is jaren geleden dat ik nog naar een festival ben geweest. Ik amuseer me."
"Het is al 50 jaar geleden dat ik me nog zo geamuseerd heb", roept Guido enthousiast. "Ik heb hier al veel schone dingen gezien. Ik kijk mijn ogen uit."
Voor Jeaninne is het zelfs een primeur: "Ik ben nog nooit op een festival geweest. Hier lopen veel schone mensen rond. Dat is leuk om te zien", zegt ze.
Front seats
De 4 bewoners krijgen front seats bij Willy Sommers. En ook daar zijn ze goed op voorbereid. "We hebben de muziek van Willy Sommers al een aantal keren opgezet in de gangen, zodat ze de teksten een beetje kennen. Ze zullen de liedjes zeker kunnen meezingen", lacht Flockmans.
Niet alleen voor de bewoners, ook voor de begeleiders is het een feestelijke dag. "Beiretof hè", zegt begeleidster Jorunn enthousiast. "Ik had normaal verlof, maar dit wilde ik niet missen. Iedereen is zich zo aan het amuseren, meer hebben we niet nodig", zegt ze nog.

title: Democrats' 2028 presidential calendar gives Black and Latino voters and union members an early say
content:
By — Mike Catalini, Associated Press Mike Catalini, Associated Press By — Bill Barrow, Associated Press Bill Barrow, Associated Press Leave your feedback Share Copy URL https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/democrats-2028-presidential-calendar-gives-black-and-latino-voters-and-union-members-an-early-say Email Facebook Twitter LinkedIn Pinterest Tumblr Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Democrats' 2028 presidential calendar gives Black and Latino voters and union members an early say Politics Aug 15, 2026 3:00 PM EDT AUSTIN, Texas (AP) — Democrats seeking the party's presidential nomination in 2028 will need to prove themselves early on in states where Black and Latino voters and union members are key supporters, under an election-year calendar approved Saturday. The primary lineup pushes Iowa from the traditional top spot and makes South Carolina the leadoff state, voting on Jan. 22, 2028, followed by Nevada on Feb. 1. New Hampshire, New Mexico, Michigan and Virginia round out the early states, throughout February, according to the plan endorsed by the Democratic National Committee at its meeting in Texas. DNC Chairman Ken Martin said that to win the general election, "You have to be battle-tested in a way that you already have campaigned in front of and for the support of various communities throughout the country." That is why the calendar designed by the party matters, he said in an interview. Some potential candidates in what is expected to be a large field have visited early-voting states such as South Carolina. Party leaders have said the order give candidates the best shot at winning back the White House after Republican President Donald Trump's second term. "They have to show that they can go to the South and talk to Black voters and rural voters, as well as out west, talking ranching and mining issues, to a border state, to union members," said party strategist Karen Finney, who has worked on multiple presidential campaigns. "Whoever survives will be battle-tested." Former presidential candidate Howard Dean, a onetime Vermont governor, recalled his tenure as national party chairman, when Democrats solidified Nevada and South Carolina as early states behind Iowa and New Hampshire. The latest change is even better, he said. "These states look more like the country," as a whole, he said, "whereas Iowa and New Hampshire don't." Nonwhite voters claim top billing As the first-in-the-South primary, South Carolina was more decisive than Iowa and New Hampshire for nominees Barack Obama in 2008, Hillary Clinton in 2016 and Joe Biden in 2020. All three dominated among South Carolina's large Black population, which can yield more than half the state's Democratic primary electorate. READ MORE: Trump's vaccine order hands some MAHA voters a win. It also gives Democrats an attack line With Nevada and New Mexico following, that will require candidates to court more Latino voters early in the process. Shifting from Iowa and New Hampshire does not mean little-known candidates cannot catch fire, as Pete Buttigieg did in Iowa and New Hampshire in 2020, when he was a 37-year-old former mayor. They just will not be able to do it with an almost entirely white audience. "If you can't go to every part of this country and make your case, you should not be running for president," Finney said. There is disagreement over how Democrats' split between progressives and mainstream liberals may or may not surface in the nominating calendar. "I think our primary voters up north are probably a little different than primary voters in South Carolina," said Boyd Brown, a former DNC member from South Carolina. "It's not the woke ideologies that we just can't get away from" in other places. Nina Smith, a former Buttigieg adviser who now works closely with progressive causes, disagreed. Smith said Black South Carolinians, especially, have gravitated to more moderate candidates – twice rejecting Vermont Sen. Bernie Sanders in favor of Clinton and Biden. READ MORE: Peggy Flanagan wins Senate primary in Minnesota, notching another victory for progressive Democrats But, she said, "Southern Black voters are more progressive than they're given credit for" on policy but also "realists" about what is possible. "Living through Jim Crow and other oppressive structures will force you to be take that approach," she said. Smith said that with South Carolina leading off and many Southern states following on Super Tuesday soon after the early lineup concludes, progressives will have to take the time to listen and then tailor their messages. "A lot of Black voters don't necessarily see themselves in the ideas and arguments that progressives put forward," she said. Unions will get a spotlight in the early-voting states Nevada has the service industry unions because of Las Vegas; Michigan has the auto industry and associated manufacturing support industries; Virginia is home to more federal workers than any other state. "Labor is still so important," Dean said. Beyond seeking the backing of organized labor, the campaigns and the party will look to unions for help in spreading Democrats' message to voters and getting people to the polls. More scheduling efficiency for candidates Campaigns struggle to balance many demands such as meeting voters in person, raising money and the logistics of travel. As a result, places such as Nevada have gotten short shrift in the past because candidates, most from the eastern part of the country, have concluded the investment of time is not worth it. An expanded calendar offers more clustering opportunities. READ MORE: Wisconsin primary offers mixed signals for Democrats, and other election takeaways A swing to the West could hit two early states — Nevada and New Mexico — and include a fundraising stop in California, full of Democratic donors. A South Carolina trip could mean fundraisers and public appearances in Atlanta, Charlotte and Raleigh, both in North Carolina. Virginia offers proximity to donors and national TV studios in Washington; the same options are available by adding a New York City stop on the way to New Hampshire. Bre Maxwell is a DNC member from South Carolina who said the state's smaller size and lower media costs are a financial equalizer, allowing not only the best-funded candidates to have an impact. "They can campaign from the top to the bottom in a day," Maxwell said. It's about primaries, with a clear look to November Of the six early states, all but South Carolina have been competitive in general elections. That means that even before Super Tuesday, the Democratic candidates will have spent significant time and resources in states worth a combined 43 Electoral College votes. That is not insignificant on the way to the 270 needed to win. Television ads and news coverage can spill over, as well. Markets targeting parts of South Carolina also reach portions of North Carolina and Georgia. After all, Brown said, the point is to put a Democrat in the White House. "This is not a social or a debate club. It is a political party," he said. Barrow reported from Atlanta. Associated Press writer Meg Kinnard in Columbia, S.C., contributed to this report. AUSTIN, Texas (AP) — Democrats seeking the party's presidential nomination in 2028 will need to prove themselves early on in states where Black and Latino voters and union members are key supporters, under an election-year calendar approved Saturday. The primary lineup pushes Iowa from the traditional top spot and makes South Carolina the leadoff state, voting on Jan. 22, 2028, followed by Nevada on Feb. 1. New Hampshire, New Mexico, Michigan and Virginia round out the early states, throughout February, according to the plan endorsed by the Democratic National Committee at its meeting in Texas.
